explanation: Emerging viruses are viruses that have recently crossed species barriers or have infected previously unaffected populations, such as H1N1 flu, West Nile virus, and COVID-19. In influenza pandemics, the viral structure features two critical surface proteins: the H (hemagglutinin) spike and the N (neuraminidase) spike. The H spike, which has 16 different types, binds to receptors on host cell membranes. The N spike, which has 9 different types, attacks host cell membranes to facilitate the exit of mature viruses. Because each type of spike has multiple varieties, the host's immune system can only recognize and defend against H and N spikes to which it has previously been exposed.
